_meta.name: Privacy-chain tracing (public sample)
_meta.description: Public SAMPLE: three tracing cases (a Zcash pool, Monero rings, a cross-chain swap). Each answer is a report, graded finding by finding against a checklist with decoys. Real sets stay private.

prompt:
Zcash. Below is every transfer between the shielded pool and the transparent addresses under investigation, over three days. Amounts are in ZEC. Nothing inside the pool is visible.

Rules of this ledger:
- A deposit credits its full amount to the shielded balance of the wallet that made it. The 0.0001 ZEC transaction fee of a deposit is paid by the transparent address on top of the amount.
- Every withdrawal pays a flat fee of 0.0001 ZEC out of the shielded balance, so a wallet that empties a balance B with n withdrawals pays out B − n × 0.0001 in total.
- A wallet can withdraw a balance in one or several parts, and one withdrawal can spend more than one of the wallet's deposits.
- The pool held funds before the window opened, and funds can stay in it after the window closes.

checklist.finding: W2 (41.87644321) is D3 (41.87654321) less one 0.0001 fee: a unique eight-decimal amount, so W2 withdraws D3
W6 + W12 + W19 = 88.1234 + 71.5 + 103.6263 = 263.2497 = D11 (263.25) less three fees: D11 was withdrawn in three parts
W5 (263.2499) equals D11 less one fee but was sent 25 minutes before D11 arrived, so it cannot come from D11; no listed deposit funds it
W10 (200.0099) = D4 (120.4) + D10 (79.61) less one fee: one wallet withdrew both deposits together, so the depositing addresses t1Dn…48 and t1Re…d7 are controlled by the same party

W4 (54.9999) withdraws D5 (55) to t1Sb…58, which deposits it again as D6 (54.9998, after the 0.0001 transaction fee), and W14 (54.9997) withdraws that: t1Sb…58 is a pass-through and the funds from t1Yz…c4 end at t1Fn…c9

The three 49.9999 withdrawals W3, W13 and W23 fit the four 50 ZEC deposits D1, D8, D12 and D16 only as a set. Timing narrows W3 to D1 (the only 50 ZEC deposit before it), but W13 and W23 have no one-to-one link, and at least one 50 ZEC deposit is still in the pool
D13 (150) is emptied by W17 (90) plus one 59.9998 withdrawal, and there are two of those, W18 and W21: the ledger cannot say which one completes D13, and the other has no source in the window
W1 is earlier than every deposit, so it spends funds that were already in the pool and cannot be linked to any listed deposit
W12 (a part of D11) and W10 (the merged D4 and D10) pay the same address t1Ab…b1: the wallet behind D11 and the wallet behind D4 and D10 pay a common recipient
D3 and D19 come from the same address t1Ln…18, so one depositor made both; D19 (18.5) has no matching withdrawal and is still in the pool at the end

The remaining withdrawals (W7, W8, W9, W11, W15, W16, W20, W22, W24, W25, W26, W27) match no deposit or combination of deposits, and the remaining deposits (D2, D7, D9, D14, D15, D17, D18, D20) have no visible exit: they cannot be linked and are reported as unexplained, not matched
Links W5 to D11 (says W5 is the withdrawal of D11)
Assigns W13 or W23 to one specific 50 ZEC deposit as an established link
States as established, not as a guess, which of W18 and W21 completes D13

T13 is one transaction with two inputs.

Chain split: the key image of T9's input also appears in a transaction on the other branch of a chain split, where it was signed with a different ring: O3, O15, O18. A key image is derived from the one output really spent, so the same key image always means the same real output.

Write the tracing report. For every input, say which output is really spent: mark it as proven when the ledger forces it and show the chain of reasoning, give the remaining candidates when it does not, and name any heuristic that favours one candidate and how far it can be trusted. Keep proven conclusions and heuristic guesses apart. Do not claim links between senders that ring membership cannot support.

checklist.finding: T1 has a ring of one member, so it provably spends O11; that removes O11 from T2, which provably spends O7, and then T3 provably spends O5
T4 is left with O10 or O1 once O7 and O5 are removed; the later single-member input T12 provably spends O1, so T4 provably spends O10: a later transaction deanonymises an earlier one

T6, T7 and T8 have only O6, O20, O21 left between them once the spent outputs O11 and O5 are removed: three inputs over three outputs, so together they spend exactly those three, but which input spends which is not proven
T5 provably spends O17: in its ring O7 is already spent and O20 and O21 are consumed by the closed set of T6, T7 and T8
The key image of T9 appears on the other branch with a different ring; the real output must be in both rings and O18 is the only common member, so T9 provably spends O18
With O18 spent by T9, T10 provably spends O22
T11 loses O18 and O22 and is left with three candidates (O13, O14, O23): not proven

In T13, input 1 is left with O2 or O12 (O1 is spent) and input 2 with O4 or O16 (O17 is spent). O2 and O16 were created by the same transaction tx-al, so the output-merging heuristic says T13 most likely spends those two: a strong guess, not proof

The newest-output heuristic favours O19 in T14 (created 50 blocks earlier): likely, not proven. In the closed set it points at O6 for both T6 and T7, which cannot both be true, so it cannot settle that set
8 of the 15 inputs are provably traced (T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, T9, T10, T12); the other 7 keep two or three candidates
Concludes that transactions share a sender because their rings share members
States as proven, not as a heuristic guess, that T13 spends O2 and O16
States as proven which single output T6, T7 or T8 spends (for example "T6 spends O6")

prompt:
Cross-chain. A cluster under investigation sells ZEC through an instant-swap service that pays out in BTC. You have the service's ledger for one afternoon, 12:00 to 18:00: every ZEC deposit it received and every BTC payout it sent, plus two later observations on Bitcoin.

How the service works:
- It logs when it first sees a deposit and when the deposit confirms. The rate is the one in force at the minute of confirmation. Rates in BTC per ZEC, each valid for 30 minutes from the time shown: 12:00 0.000840, 12:30 0.000843, 13:00 0.000851, 13:30 0.000848, 14:00 0.000855, 14:30 0.000862, 15:00 0.000870, 15:30 0.000866, 16:00 0.000859, 16:30 0.000861, 17:00 0.000868, 17:30 0.000872.
- The service fee is 0.5% for a deposit under 500 ZEC and 0.4% for a deposit of 500 ZEC or more. Payout = deposit × rate × (1 − service fee) − 0.00012 BTC network fee, rounded down to 8 decimals.
- A payout is sent 10 to 20 minutes after its deposit confirms, and a deposit is paid out at most once.
- Batching: two deposits from the same sending address that confirm within 5 minutes of each other are paid in one payout. Each is priced on its own (own rate, own service fee), the two results are added and the network fee is charged once. The payout is sent 10 to 20 minutes after the second one confirms.
- A payout above 1 BTC is sent as two transactions to the same address: exactly 1.00000000 BTC, then the remainder 1 to 3 minutes later.
- Deposits under 5 ZEC are not swapped. They are refunded in ZEC.
- The service also takes other coins, so a BTC payout does not have to come from a ZEC deposit.

Match every payout to its deposit or deposits with the arithmetic, resolve or flag any ambiguity, account for every deposit and every payout that is left over, and state what the addresses and the later observations do and do not let you conclude about who controls the funds.

checklist.finding: The one-to-one swaps: B2 (0.10017600) pays Z1 (120 ZEC at 0.000840), B6 (0.08455450) pays Z5 (100 ZEC at 0.000851), B7 (0.08455450) pays Z6 (100 ZEC at 0.000851), B17 (0.06472066) pays Z13 (75.25 ZEC at 0.000866), B21 (0.20500920) pays Z17 (240 ZEC at 0.000859), B23 (0.55317792) pays Z19 (640 ZEC at 0.000868), B24 (0.02838078) pays Z20 (33 ZEC at 0.000868) (credit when at least five of the seven are matched correctly)

B3, B4 and B5 carry the same amount (0.25193489, a 300.5 ZEC deposit at 0.000843) and there are three such deposits. The 10 to 20 minute rule resolves them: B3 (12:48) can only pay Z2, which leaves B4 to Z3 and B5 to Z4
Z5 and Z6 come from the same address but confirm 7 minutes apart, so they are not batched: each gets its own payout (B6 and B7), both to bc1q…ala

Z7 (180 ZEC, confirmed 13:27 at 0.000851) and Z8 (220 ZEC, confirmed 13:31 at 0.000848) come from the same address within 5 minutes, so they are paid together: 180 × 0.000851 × 0.995 + 220 × 0.000848 × 0.995 − 0.00012 = 0.33792130, which is B9
Z9 is exactly 500 ZEC, so it pays the 0.4% fee: 500 × 0.000848 × 0.996 − 0.00012 = 0.42218400, which is B10
Z10 was first seen at 14:27 but confirmed at 14:31, so it gets the 14:30 rate: 75.25 × 0.000862 × 0.995 − 0.00012 = 0.06442117, paid by B13 at 14:44

B12 (0.06389705) is what 75.25 ZEC would pay at the 14:00 rate, but no 75.25 ZEC deposit confirmed in that half hour, Z10 is paid by B13, and B12 is sent only 9 minutes after Z10 confirmed: no ZEC deposit explains B12
Z11 (1,500 ZEC at 0.000870, 0.4% fee) pays 1.29966000 BTC, above 1 BTC, so it is sent in two parts to the same address: B14 (1.00000000) and B15 (0.29966000)
B18 pays Z14 at the 15:30 rate, because Z14 confirmed at 15:57 although the payout left at 16:10, and at the 0.4% fee: 512.33 × 0.000866 × 0.996 − 0.00012 = 0.44178306

Z15 and Z16 are both 250 ZEC at the same rate, and B19 and B20 carry the same amount (0.21355625) to two different addresses; both payouts fall inside both payout windows, so the ledger cannot say which payout belongs to which deposit
Z12 (4.2 ZEC) is under the 5 ZEC minimum, so it was refunded and has no BTC payout; it was sent from the same address as Z17 (t1…8uk), so one actor made both
Z18 (88.8 ZEC) confirmed at 16:48, so its payout was due by 17:08, inside the ledger, and there is none: it is unpaid (held, failed or frozen) and should be flagged
Z21 (60 ZEC) confirmed at 17:48, so its payout can come any time from 17:58 to 18:08 and the ledger ends at 18:00: the payout is not overdue and nothing can be concluded from its absence
B1, B8, B11, B16, B22, B25 match no ZEC deposit and were funded by other coins; that includes B22, exactly 1.00000000 BTC with no remainder after it, which is not the first half of a split payout

The coins from B2, B14 and B15 are spent together in one transaction (common-input ownership), so one party controls both payout addresses and the Z1 and Z11 deposits, 1,620 ZEC, belong to the same actor

B13 was paid to an exchange deposit address (many unrelated depositors, hourly sweeps to cold storage): custody passes to the exchange, the on-chain trail ends there and identifying the account needs the exchange's records
B3 and B5 go to the same address bc1q…l9a, so one recipient received the Z2 and Z4 swaps (601 ZEC); B4 went to a different address
Matches B12 to Z10, or says Z10 was paid twice
Attributes the exchange address's other depositors, or the exchange's cold wallet, to the cluster under investigation
Reports Z21 as unpaid or overdue in the same way as Z18
States as established, not as a guess, which of B19 and B20 pays Z15
